_note: Round 22. Closes all four of round 21's e-GDDS 'group 1' leads (Burundi, Djibouti, Guinea, Central African Republic -- int-imf-egdds-oda-round21-2026-09-08.json's _dropped, which found no NSDP tab in each country's opendataforafrica.org portal nav and, for CAR, no portal at all under the slug tried). The fix in every case was the same: the IMF's own press release announcing that country's e-GDDS implementation (found via WebSearch, read in Chrome since www.imf.org 403s to curl per notes/imf-dsbb-2026-09-06.md) links DIRECTLY to the country's real NSDP page -- which exists at a URL the portal's own nav does not surface (Burundi: a random slug; Djibouti/Guinea: a short /nsdp path; CAR: the slug is 'car', not 'centrafrique' as round 21 guessed). All four NSDP pages carry the identical self-declared boilerplate rounds 19-21 established, all four graded A on the first attempt. Generalisable finding for the seven group-2 (non-African) countries or any future e-GDDS gap: when a country's opendataforafrica.org portal has no visible NSDP tab, check the IMF's own press release for that country's e-GDDS launch before concluding no page exists -- it typically links straight to it. No id or evidence-URL collision against the whole corpus for any of the four new nodes or URLs (checked before writing). All four countries' ISO codes (BI, DJ, GN, CF) already have live nodes elsewhere in the corpus, so no new COUNTRY_FAMILY/CONTINENT_OF/COUNTRY_LABEL entries are needed.
